svg.title: PetaJournal architecture: clients, local server, storage and sync
svg.desc: The libraries of the frontend side begin with client-. client-core was peta-core. The packages of the apps have the names of the apps (ADR 040): outliner-web was client-shell-leptos, and outliner-emacs was client-shell-emacs. Six frontends share one core. The four native apps have the same shape. Each has a shell crate at the entrance. It is the entrance of BoltFFI, and it gives client-native-bridge an implementation of Host. client-native-bridge has the Host trait and carries events and effects as bytes between client-core and the app. It was shell-native. The Host of a shell crate calls an API crate. The WinUI frontend is stickies-win (C#, WinUI), and the SwiftUI frontend is stickies-mac (Swift, SwiftUI). Both are connected by bincode over BoltFFI to a Rust library with client-shell-http, client-native-bridge, client-core and client-api-http (Rust, ureq). client-shell-http is new: it has what shell-native had for the journal server. client-api-http was server-client. It talks to the local server with REST and SSE. The Android frontend is outliner-android (Kotlin, Compose), and the iOS frontend is outliner-ios (Swift, SwiftUI). Both are connected by bincode over BoltFFI to a Rust library with client-shell-embedded, client-native-bridge, client-core, client-api-embedded and journal-core. client-shell-embedded was shell-android. client-api-embedded was embedded-journal. It asks no server: it calls journal-core, the inside of the journal server, in the same library. journal-core keeps a SQLite database in the app and syncs the pages with the .md files of a folder of the app, in both directions. The Kotlin side and the Swift side download and upload those files with the Dropbox SDK. client-core parses the Markdown of an item with flatmarkdown. It puts the AST, a Node of flatmarkdown-ast, into the row of the view model. The types of the four native apps are generated from the Node, in C#, Swift and Kotlin. Each native app draws an item from that type with the parts of its OS. The browser frontend is one WASM binary with outliner-web (Rust, Leptos) and client-core (Rust, Crux), and talks to the server with fetch and EventSource. It shows an item from the HTML that flatmarkdown-ast2html makes of the AST of the row, and adds the link targets, the image sizes and the code colours itself. The Emacs frontend is peta-journal.el (Emacs Lisp), connected by JSON lines over stdin and stdout to a Rust process with outliner-emacs, client-core and client-api-http. Two more frontends do not use the core. The todo frontend (TypeScript, React) talks to the server with fetch and EventSource, and renders the AST with flatmarkdown-ast2react, a TypeScript package. The memoview frontend (C#, WinUI) talks to the server with HttpClient, and renders the AST with flatmarkdown-ast2html. The arrows from the server to todo and to memoview carry the AST of an item: these two draw from the AST and do not read the Markdown. The arrow to the AI agent carries the Markdown of an item. The arrows to the four frontends that use client-core and ask the server carry the Markdown too: client-core does not read the AST of the answer. A label in a gray envelope on an arrow names the main data that the arrow carries. It does not say in which direction. The bincode arrows of the four native apps carry the AST: it is in the rows of the view model. The pipe of the Emacs frontend carries the Markdown: Emacs shows it as it is. In the iOS and Android apps, client-api-embedded gets the Markdown from journal-core with a function call. The local server has two parts. journal-server (Rust, axum) serves REST and SSE at /api/events. It also serves MCP at /mcp. It calls journal-core (Rust) in the same process. journal-core keeps the pages in a SQLite database. It syncs the pages with .md files in a local folder outside the server, in both directions. That arrow carries Markdown. Dropbox, a cloud storage service, may sync that folder with remote machines and with the mobile apps. A box below the cloud storage stands for the remote machines and the mobile devices. An AI agent talks to it as an MCP client over Streamable HTTP. Astro makes a web site from the .md files of the local folder. That arrow carries Markdown too. The folders of .md files are painted yellow. The local server is painted gray. A ribbon of one colour joins the boxes of one crate. The purple ribbon joins client-core of all six frontends. The pink ribbon joins client-native-bridge of the four native apps. The olive ribbon joins client-shell-http of Windows and macOS. The blue ribbon joins client-shell-embedded of iOS and Android. The green ribbon joins client-api-http of Emacs, Windows and macOS. The teal ribbon joins client-api-embedded of iOS and Android. The orange ribbon joins journal-core of the server, of iOS and of Android. A box below the notes says what client-core is responsible for. It has no screen: it takes events from the shell, and answers with effects and a view model. It does not rewrite the items. journal-core does that in one transaction: split, merge, paste, move, indent and the task state. client-core turns one operation of the user into one request, and puts the answer into the state of the screen. It decides which operation a key or a click means: Enter splits an item, adds a line inside a code fence, or outdents an empty last item. It builds the request, with the text that is not saved yet, and the way to read the answer. The shell sends it. It shows the answer: it rewrites the state of the screen, places the cursor and records the undo. Indent and collapsing are shown before the answer comes. It keeps the state of the screen: the tree of the outline, the selection, the cursor, the unsaved text and the history of undo and redo. It saves typed text after a short pause, and takes in the changes of other clients and of the .md files. It has the logic of the screens: the route, the journal, a page, the sidebar, search, settings, the atlas and the names for a wiki link. It makes the view model again after every event, and parses the Markdown of each item for the AST of its row. A second box below it lists the flatmarkdown libraries. A dark chip on a box names a flatmarkdown crate that the box uses. A white chip with the word ast on a native app stands for the types generated from the Node.

g.text: Webアプリ（アウトライナー & アトラス）
Emacsのメジャーモード（アウトライナー）
Windowsネイティブアプリ（付箋紙）
リンク・画像・色付けを補う
行を描画・操作を送信
ネイティブ描画・操作を送信
FFIの入口・Hostの実装を注入
macOSネイティブアプリ（付箋紙）
ネイティブ描画・操作を送信
iOSネイティブアプリ（アウトライナー）
ネイティブ描画・操作を送信
FFIの入口・Hostの実装を注入
Androidネイティブアプリ（アウトライナー）
ネイティブ描画・操作を送信
DB・同期・検索・拡張関数
タスクを一覧・状態を
切り替えできるWebアプリ
ページを付箋紙として表示
できるデスクトップアプリ
ページを検索・読み書き
その他のWebアプリ群、WebViewアプリ群は手軽に増やせるタイプのクライアントです。Readが中心の単純な形で、client-coreを使わずにサーバと直接話します。
画面を持たない、フロントエンドの共通ロジックです。シェルからEventを受け取り、Effect（シェルへの頼みごと）とViewModel（VM、画面に出す内容）を返します。
通信・タイマー・描画は自分では行わず、シェルに頼みます。
項目の書き換えは、client-coreの責務ではありません。分割・結合・貼り付け・移動・字下げ・タスクの状態は、journal-coreが1つのトランザクションで書き換えます。
client-coreは、利用者の1つの操作を1つの要求にして頼み、返ってきた結果を画面の状態へ反映させます。
画像はclient-coreを通らず、画面を描くコードがローカルサーバから直接読みます。iOSとAndroidはアプリ内フォルダから読みます。
キーやクリックが、どの操作にあたるかを決めます。たとえばEnterは、項目の分割、コードの中の改行、空の末尾の項目の字下げ解除のどれかになります。
1つの操作を、サーバへの書き込み要求1つにします。未保存の本文も、その要求に載せます。RESTのリクエストと応答の読み方を作り、送るのはシェルに任せます。
サーバから返ってきた結果を画面の状態へ反映させ、カーソルの行き先を決め、Undoの記録を作ります。字下げと折りたたみは操作感を高めるため、結果を待たずに先に画面を変えます。
アウトラインの木、選択範囲、カーソルの位置、未保存の本文、Undo・Redoの履歴を持ちます。Undoは手元で変更を戻し、サーバには1つの要求で伝えます。
打った文字を、少し待ってから自動で保存します。ほかのクライアントや.mdファイルの変更を取り込みます。
URLに合わせた画面の切り替え、ジャーナル、ページ、サイドバー、検索、設定、アトラス、Wikiリンクの補完を受け持ちます。
イベントのたびにViewModelを作り直します。Markdownを解析して行ごとのAST（Node）を作り、見出しの大きさ、タスクの状態、字下げ、日付の見出しを決めます。
アウトライナー向けのMarkdown（Flat Markdown形式）をASTへパース
Nodeから生成した型（C#, Swift, Kotlin）
ネイティブのシェルが受け取って描く型
